head: cloud/http-expect-continue
title: fix(serve): answer Expect: 100-continue before reading the body
body:
> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; an independent Claude Fable 5.1 review approved it before submission; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope: CPU only, on a 4-core x86-64 cloud VM with no GPU (`cmake --preset cpu-test`, GCC). The new `TestExpectContinue` in `http_server_test` fails on `main` without the fix (`Assertion 'count > 0' failed`: no interim response arrives within the test socket's 3 s receive timeout) and passes with it. `cmake --build --preset pr` passed (100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 59). `nix shell --inputs-from . nixpkgs#clang-tools -c python3 tools/ci/check-format.py` passes. No model, server or GPU runs. Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

## Problem

curl adds `Expect: 100-continue` to any request body over 1 MiB, for example an image or audio upload with `-F file=@...` or `--data-binary @file`. It then holds the body back until the server answers `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue`, or until its 1 s `expect_100_timeout` runs out. `HttpServer::handle_connection` never looks at `Expect` and goes straight to reading the body, so each such upload waits that extra second before curl sends anything. RFC 9110 §10.1.1 requires a server that receives `100-continue` in an HTTP/1.1 request either to send a 100 response or to send a final status.

Measured with curl 8.5.0 against a minimal local stand-in server (Python, not Gufo):

| Body | `Expect` sent | No 100 reply | 100 reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,048,576 bytes | no | 0.007 s | - |
| 1,048,577 bytes | yes | 1.004 s | - |
| 2,000,000 bytes | yes | 1.007 s | 0.015 s |

## Change

When an HTTP/1.1 request has an accepted `Content-Length` and its body has not fully arrived yet, and it carries `Expect: 100-continue` (header name and value case-insensitive), the server sends `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` before reading the rest of the body. Everything else is unchanged:

- An oversized body still gets its final 413 without a 100 first. The test covers this.
- Malformed framing still gets 400.
- An HTTP/1.0 request's expectation is ignored, as RFC 9110 requires.
- No 100 is sent when the body has already arrived in full.

The test sends only the headers, checks that the interim response arrives before any body bytes, then sends the body and expects the echoed 200. It runs once with `Expect: 100-continue` and once with lowercase `expect: 100-Continue`.

review.summary: Change is correct and minimal: case-insensitive Expect match, HTTP/1.1 only, 413 still final without a 100, no 100 when body already arrived, SendAll failure handled like ReadN failure, one-request-per-connection semantics unaffected. Test is deterministic, provably fails on main and passes with the fix. Reran http_server_test and the full cpu-test CTest suite (123/123 passed), pinned clang-format 21.1.8 passes, PR title check passes, diff matches the patch exactly. Every body claim is backed by evidence; test scope is CPU only; AI disclosure is the first line naming Claude Opus 5.5 developer and Claude Fable 5.1 reviewer; no secrets, hosts, IPs or profession hints.
